comments.value: So I'm talking to Content Creators and Veterans of the Game / Community. I shall -ofc with their permission- share their input while maintaining privacy, here.
I want to meet people and be myself. I want to record content and be able to be in the model I created for myself without the fear of someone forcefully taking it away from me. Please VRchat.

details:
The ripping and theft sadly will never stop. Even Triple A game titles get their content stolen / ripped.
Sadly  VRC API is very open and anyone can download any avatar or world, fairly easily. Which is sad.
As of right now, there are more and more malicious clients going about. Most of them have a shit ton of back doors that their users don't even know about. God have mercy on you if you bought one of those using a Credit Card.
If we want to stop or minimize the threat of rippers. We'd have to start at the root of the problem.
It's not Mod makers. Its the API and Engine VRC works on. Anyone with decent knowledge about Unity and writing Code can make clients or mods for this game, sadly.
Which is a bad but also a good thing. As many know, there are harmless mods too!
Mods that just improve the game without interrupting other peoples experience.
Or posing a threat to others.
If they really want to add monetization in to the game, they absolutely must find a way to secure content uploaded to VRC and take more serious measures against theft.
Anyone who made a world knows, that you get moderation TOOLs.
A way to fix theft or at the very least put a massive (but probably not permanent) stop to this.
Is to remove the ability to upload avatars directly without removing complete customization of avatars somehow.
I'm thinking of a Avatar Hub. A in game a-like store / wardrobe. To which you can not directly upload but you can pick any Public avatar within it.
You can wear them and use them but to make Updates or Changes on it, you'd have to buy it.  
Buying avatars in game can be traced by VRChat then and should offer more protection. Not only that it also allows for refunds since they could delete the avatar from your Avatar Hub account.
Users electable to purchase avatars I would say would start at the "New User" Rank. 
Anyone seen abusing an avatar can easily be moderated or should be easily managed. 
This way VRChat has control over what's uploaded and by who. 
People that can upload should at the very least be Users with an VRC account. No pure Quest or Steam users.
So you need a VRC account and it would have to be linked to the Avatar Hub. You can only link 1 account to the Avatar Hub, there for if one would upload stolen content. VRChat in theory could terminate not just their "free" VRC account but also the Account connected to the Avatar Hub, which in terms would delete ALL avatars connected to it. 
This would I believe discourage theft and ripping by a lot I believe. 
Since you can't directly upload from unity without a linked account. 
Edits to avatars you bought can only made public if the original creator of the avatar allows it.
Those public avatars can also not be reuploaded as easily as before since, even if you would rip a public avatar. 
Trying to upload an avatar you do not own with your linked account would count as a new entry, thus. It should be fairly obvious in the Data Base to find similar avatar bases and figure out with an algorithm if or who owns that base. 
Yes i know, this is a lot more complicated than I make it sound. But i believe THIS is how we could stop theft or at least make it very hard.
Even if people would steal content, they could not just simply reupload it without hindrance. 
VRChat could there for make use of something similar to CS:GO Overwatch and have trusted (Legendary or Veteran Users) and Content creators look over Avatar uploads and help VRC Staff by marking Uploads as potential stolen content.
Those users would not have the power to deny uploads and it would be voluntary but it could improve the security of Unique content by a lot. And they could be rewarded with VRC Plus or something a-like based on how accurate their judgement is, perhaps.
It would also encourage more interaction between VRC and its community!
I have no idea how to write Code but I think this is worth discussing. At least i have not seen any one else bring this up.
Thank you for reading, please let us/me know what you think about this! 
Side Note: Anything in my suggestion or Idea is "Subject to change" and none of it is final ofc. But i think, this could work.
title: Content Protection & Interaction between VRC and its Community!
